sections.title: The letter esse
paragraphs: The name of this letter is (esse) /ɛs/. Its main sound is in (sac) /sak/, which means bag. This letter makes two spoken sounds. It can also stay quiet.

sections.title: Making the sounds
paragraphs: For the first sound, place your tongue tip near your upper gum. Push air out through a narrow gap to make a hiss. Touch your throat to feel that it does not shake. For the second sound, keep the same mouth shape, but turn your voice on. Touch your throat to feel the shaking.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: At the start of a word or next to another consonant, you hear the hiss in (poste) /pɔst/. Between two vowels, the sound turns into a buzz, as in (rose) /ʁoz/. At the end of many words, this letter is a silent letter, so you do not pronounce it at all in (bras) /bʁa/.

sections.title: Common mistakes
paragraphs: Do not voice the final sound when it stands alone at the end of a word. Many learners say the buzz of English buzz in (temps) /tɑ̃/. Remember that the end stays silent. Another trap is forgetting to turn on your voice between two vowels. Do not hiss like the sound in sun when you say (base) /baz/.
